text:
VIENNA — Uganda is in talks with European Union countries about hosting a hub for rejected asylum-seekers, a senior official from the African nation told POLITICO.
On Monday, five EU countries — Austria, Denmark, Germany, Greece and the Netherlands — announced plans to start deportations to a center in Rwanda from next year.
On Tuesday, Vincent Waiswa Bagiire, permanent secretary to Uganda’s foreign affairs ministry, confirmed that his country was interested in hosting a return hub.
Bagiire said Uganda had a “discussion” with the Netherlands but “we haven’t got far.” He didn’t say which other countries Uganda had been speaking with but said the talks were not that advanced: “Let me say that the discussion is at a stage of a cup of coffee.”
In June, European diplomats said Uganda and Uzbekistan were being discussed as potential locations for EU migration centers. However, Uganda has three criteria that need to be met before it can host a hub, Bagiire said on the sidelines of a conference in Vienna hosted by the International Centre for Migration Policy Development.
“If we are to establish a hub, it will be strictly for people of African origin; they should not have a criminal record; [and] no unaccompanied minors,” he said.
He added that the discussions involve “no more than 50” people, who would be sent to open facilities. “No detention, they’re not prisons — at all. People can integrate within the communities … they’re free to do whatever they need to do. The same way we treat our refugees,” he said.
